updates.title: Google Cloud sends agent telemetry to BigQuery for governance
updates.whatChanged: Google Cloud now sends first-party agent telemetry plus optional custom-agent traces, metrics, and transcripts to customer-owned BigQuery tables. BigQuery and Looker dashboards track usage, cost, and evaluation results. Conversation logging is generally available; daily token quotas and some eval tools stay in preview.
updates.whyCare: Teams can study agent latency, token use, and, when allowed, conversation content with warehouse data. Review access and retention before you log prompts and answers; Google skips transcripts for data with row- or column-level security or masking.
updates.before: Teams had no shared BigQuery path for first-party and custom-agent telemetry, logs, and evaluation results.
updates.after: First-party and custom-agent telemetry can land in BigQuery with opted-in transcripts, token use, and evaluation results.
updates.learn: Compare the BigQuery path with your current agent-analytics stack before you instrument agents twice. Set access and retention for log tables. Use byte-scan caps and preview token quotas to bound spend.

sources.name: Google Cloud Blog - New AI agent observability and governance across BigQuery and Looker
Google Cloud Docs - Conversation logging overview

updates.architectureImplication: BigQuery can act as the customer-owned analytics store for first-party and instrumented third-party agent traces, opted-in transcripts, and cost data. Keep transcript logs behind separate IAM and retention controls and plan for preview limits.
heldReasons: Fact check: The item says custom-agent transcripts can be sent to BigQuery. | The sources describe custom-agent traces and telemetry, but only describe transcript logging for first-party conversational analytics agents.

Fact check: The item says teams previously had no shared BigQuery path for first-party and custom-agent telemetry, logs, and evaluation results. | The sources announce the new framework but do not establish that teams previously lacked such a path.

updates.title: GitHub retires six Copilot models on 14 December
updates.whatChanged: GitHub says Copilot will retire Claude Fable 5, Claude Haiku 4.5, Gemini 3.8 Flash, Gemini 4 Argon, Grok 4.6, and Kimi K3 on 14 December. It recommends replacements for five models; Kimi's alternative is pending. Default model policies enable suggested replacements unless admins override them.
updates.whyCare: Teams that use these models need to test replacements and update model policies before the deadline. GitHub has not named a successor for Kimi K3, which may affect continuity for teams that rely on it.
updates.before: Copilot users could choose these models in supported experiences, subject to plan and model policies.
updates.after: On 14 December, Copilot will retire the six models across chat, inline edits, ask and agent modes, and code completions. Default policies enable suggested replacements unless admins override them.
updates.learn: Inventory Copilot model policies and workflows that use these models. Test replacements before 14 December, and plan a fallback for Kimi K3 because GitHub has not named its successor.

sources.name: GitHub Changelog - Upcoming deprecation of selected GitHub Copilot models in December
GitHub Docs - Supported AI models in GitHub Copilot

updates.architectureImplication: Treat hosted models as versioned dependencies. Keep tests ready so you can switch models before a vendor retires one, and validate a fallback when GitHub has not announced a successor.

action.what: Test replacement models and update Copilot model policies before deprecation.

heldReasons: Fact check: The item says all six models will be retired without exception. | The source exempts Claude Haiku 4.5 for individual subscribers on annual plans.

Fact check: The item presents automatic enablement of replacement models as universal. | The source limits automatic enablement to Enterprise and Business customers and notes that admins can turn off the global default or disable a model.
